claims.text: Overall wear resistance in FeNiCrCoCu coatings during high-temperature sliding is governed by formation of a continuous, adherent, self-healing surface oxide layer.
The surface oxide layer governs microscopic deformation during high-temperature sliding.
The oxide layer limits direct metal-metal contact.
The oxide layer redistributes interfacial stress.
The oxide layer mediates subsurface grain refinement or dynamic recrystallization.
Oxide-mediated refinement shifts the dominant deformation mechanism from dislocation-based plasticity toward grain-boundary sliding.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating is homogeneous and single-phase.
The as-deposited coating exhibits minimal surface oxidation under ambient conditions.
Annealing the coating in air at approximately 500°C for one hour will encourage formation of a continuous protective oxide layer.
Oxidation kinetics are appreciable during sliding at approximately 500°C in ambient air.
The resulting oxide film is likely enriched in chromium and iron.
A dense, continuous oxide film coupled with subsurface grain refinement mitigates localized deformation.
Pre-oxidation reduces abrasive wear and friction by reducing direct interaction between the coating and counter-body.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have lower wear rates than as-deposited coatings during sliding at approximately 500°C.
Pre-oxidized coatings will develop a more uniform wear track than the baseline coatings.
Pre-oxidized coatings will exhibit reduced depth and severity of subsurface plastic deformation.
Reduced subsurface deformation will be associated with finer, more uniform grains and less severe localized shear.
The predicted behavior should hold near 500°C when oxidation is appreciable but oxide spallation and wholesale coating microstructure alteration are limited.
